title: Governance Physics: testing Latency-Metric Duality on REAL committed networks, and testing the entanglement inference that the framework asserts (pre-registered and hash-locked BEFORE any gate was computed)
what_this_does_and_does_not_test: This tests the LAYER-1 content of the RT->Governance crossover applied to physics: whether a genuine distance metric emerges from a pure information-coupling matrix on REAL networks, whether its scaling exponent matches the framework's sharp prediction, and whether the framework's own inference about entanglement survives contact with its own formalism. It does NOT test, and cannot test, whether physical spacetime is a rendered interface, whether the universe is a computation, or whether observation is a rendering instruction. Those are Layer-3 framings; no dataset here adjudicates them and none is claimed to.
why_the_existing_lmd_result_is_not_enoug: physics-agency/lmd already reports a metric with zero triangle violations and a median scaling slope of ~-0.5 on SEEDED RANDOM networks. Under this repository's own simulator rule, a seeded random ensemble constructed to exhibit a property cannot be evidence that the property holds of anything real. This spec therefore re-runs the same locked claims on REAL, COMMITTED substrates -- the live PyPI dependency graph (N=540, spec 4e83893b) and the STRING v12 yeast interactome channel (N=4825) -- where the structure was measured, not generated.
the_category_error_being_tested_head_on: IMPORTANT AND DELIBERATE. The framework asserts: entangled particles are perfectly correlated, therefore their round-trip information latency tau_rt is exactly zero, therefore under d^2 = kappa * tau_rt their proper distance is exactly zero. This inference is tested here because it is CHECKABLE INSIDE THE FRAMEWORK'S OWN FORMALISM, independent of any physics. In the framework, tau_rt is realised as commute time / effective resistance on the coupling graph -- a round-TRIP transport quantity. The claim is equivalent to asserting that maximal pairwise correlation forces commute time to zero. GP5 tests exactly that on real graphs. If maximally coupled real pairs have strictly positive commute distance, the inference is refuted ON ITS OWN TERMS, and no appeal to physics interpretation can rescue it. DECLARED EXPECTATION: it will be refuted, because correlation and transport latency are different quantities -- which is also precisely why no-signalling holds in physics: perfect correlation transmits zero bits.

substrates.pypi: data/pypi/dep_graph_{nodes,edges}.csv -- 540 real packages, 1287 internal dependency edges, depth 3, fetched from the live registry under spec 4e83893b and committed. Coupling = adjacency.
substrates.yeast: biomedical-agency/data/yeast_channel_frozen.json -- the committed STRING v12 derived channel, N=4825, whose raw-file hash is checked against the frozen provenance. Coupling = the two-hop fidelity product D_enc * D_dec per node, used to build a weighted similarity graph.

definitions.coupling_matrix: W, symmetric, non-negative, zero diagonal. Built from the real edge set (PyPI) or from real per-node fidelity similarity (yeast). No coordinates are used anywhere; the graph carries no positions.
definitions.tau_rt: round-trip information latency, realised as the COMMUTE TIME between i and j on W, equivalently (up to a constant) the effective resistance R(i,j) of the graph viewed as a resistor network. This is the framework's own operationalisation.
definitions.d: emergent distance, d(i,j) = sqrt(kappa * tau_rt(i,j)) with kappa = 1. Effective resistance is a known metric, so the metric axioms are a REAL check on the implementation and on the graph being connected -- not a tautology about the definition.

gates.GP1_metric_emerges_on_a_real_graph: On the real PyPI graph's largest connected component, the induced d must satisfy the metric axioms: symmetry, zero self-distance, strict positivity off-diagonal, and the triangle inequality across a large sample of triples. PASS iff zero violations over at least 200000 sampled triples. CAN FAIL -- a disconnected component, a numerical blow-up, or a coding error all fail it.
gates.GP2_the_metric_is_not_just_degree: The emergent distance must carry structure beyond raw capacity. Compare d against a degree-only baseline: PASS iff the Spearman correlation between d(i,j) and the simple function 1/sqrt(deg_i * deg_j) is below 0.90 in magnitude, i.e. the metric is not a relabelling of degree. CAN FAIL, and a failure would mean the 'emergent geometry' is just capacity in disguise.
gates.GP3_the_scaling_exponent_matches_the_sha: THE SHARP TEST. Scale the whole coupling matrix by a factor s over a decade and regress log(mean d) on log(s). The framework predicts a slope of exactly -0.5000. PASS iff the fitted slope lies in [-0.52, -0.48] AND R^2 >= 0.999 on the REAL graph. FALSIFIABLE: any other exponent refutes the specific prediction, and it is reported with its exact value.
gates.GP4_a_degree_preserving_null_destroys_th: Rewire the real graph preserving the degree sequence (seeded, 10 x |E| double-edge swaps) and recompute. The real graph's mean distance must differ from the rewired null by more than 3 null standard deviations. PASS iff so. CAN FAIL: if a degree-preserving null reproduces the geometry, the 'emergent structure' is an artifact of the degree sequence alone.
gates.GP5_maximal_coupling_does_NOT_imply_zero: THE CATEGORY-ERROR GATE. Take the most strongly coupled real pairs (top decile by edge weight, or by fidelity similarity). The framework's entanglement inference requires their tau_rt -- and hence d -- to be zero. PASS iff their MINIMUM d is STRICTLY POSITIVE, i.e. the inference is REFUTED on the framework's own formalism. DECLARED IN ADVANCE: passing this gate means the framework's entanglement claim is WRONG. This gate is written so the framework can lose, and the expected outcome is that it does.
gates.GP6_the_exponent_replicates_on_a_second_: Repeat GP3 on the committed yeast channel. PASS iff the fitted slope again lies in [-0.52, -0.48]. CAN FAIL -- and given that the two-hop fidelity construct has already flipped sign between substrates elsewhere in this repository, cross-substrate replication is genuinely uncertain.
gates.GP7_no_layer_3_claim_is_scored: META-GATE. Every claim about rendered spacetime, observation-as-rendering, conscious processors or the universe as computation must be absent from the scored gates and present only as declared Layer-3 framing. PASS iff the results file contains no scored gate referencing those notions. DECLARED falsifiable:false -- it is a completeness check on the report, enforced by construction, and EXCLUDED from the score. It exists so the physics interpretation can never quietly acquire empirical support.

symmetric_null: Every exponent, correlation, distance and violation count is reported with its exact value whether or not it favours the framework. GP1-GP6 are genuinely at risk. GP5 is written so that the framework's own assertion is the thing that fails. GP7 is declared non-falsifiable and excluded from the score. No threshold in this file may move after the lock.
what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_mean: Passing GP1-GP4 and GP6 would establish that a genuine, non-trivial distance metric with a specific scaling exponent emerges from pure coupling on real measured networks, and that the result is not an artifact of degree or of seeded random construction. That is a real Layer-1 network-science finding about GRAPHS. It would NOT establish anything about physical spacetime, quantum mechanics, entanglement, observation, or consciousness. The word 'physics' in this directory's name refers to the FRAMEWORK being tested, not to a claim that these graphs are physical systems.
acceptance: GREEN when this spec re-hashes to its published canonical SHA-256, both substrates re-hash to their committed manifests, and every gate is evaluated exactly as written -- with misses recorded, asserted in tests, and carried into the README. Exit 0 means 'reproduces including its failures', never 'Governance Physics is validated'.
